incidents.claim_en: The official length of the Finnish-Russian border is 17 kilometres, of which 1 kilometre is land border.
Both the Soviet Union in 1939 and Finland in 1941 unilaterally abrogated their respective peace treaties by launching attacks, and Finland was forced to cede territories in 1940 and 1944.

Part of the Finnish-Norwegian border can be defined as belonging to Finland's eastern border, and the Russian border zone is wider than the Finnish one, where a permit requires a justified reason from the Border Guard.
The Finnish Border Guard's military organization is controversial among security authorities and its military training is often insufficient for law enforcement tasks.
The Russian-side border crossing point at Vaalimaa is named Ylä-Urpala.
Both the Soviet Union in 1939 and Finland in 1941 unilaterally broke their peace treaties, and Finland was forced to cede territories in 1940 and 1944 while selling Jäniskoski-Niskakoski in 1947.

The Soviet Union existed from 30 December 1922 until 25 December 1991, when its first president resigned and the central government lost its constitutional actor, making the Russian Federation the state east of the border.
